marta: OK team — finalizing the benchmark narrative for next week's launch. Need a short decision: do we lead with tokens-per-dollar (cost-efficiency framing) or p99-latency (SLA reliability framing)? I sketched three chart concepts in Figma: link https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/throughput-storyline

devin: My gut says tokens-per-dollar for top-funnel content, p99 for enterprise followups. keep it simple for the hero chart.

kai: agree. can we combine into a small 2x1 panel? hero = tokens/dollar, inset = p99 vs model-size. quick sketch ->

kai: ```
hero: x=tokens/s, y=dollars per 1M tokens
inset: x=model size, y=p99 latency (ms)
```

olivia: For webinar promo copy — lead with a concrete savings claim. e.g., "Cut inference cost 3x while keeping <100ms p95". we should be conservative though, back with data.

marta: good call. devin can you pull the slice that supports "3x"? short table will work for a slide.

devin: on it. pulling variants: quantized-A vs reference. will post numbers in a minute.

deploy-bot: scheduled benchmark run started (job 9981) — ETA 12m.

kai: inbound routing note — we'll have two CTAs: "Try hosted API" and "Get Dedicated quote". route clicks on the latter to sales@redwood.com with utm=dedicated_bench

olivia: Also suggest a short checklist for the SDRs: 1) mention p99 SLA 2) cite tokens-per-dollar table 3) offer benchmarks.pdf link. I'll draft.

marta: perfect. last ask: visual tone — prefer clean line charts (no 3D), annotate points where caching/batching applies. folks, react with :thumbsup: if you approve the hero as tokens-per-dollar + inset p99.

devin: :thumbsup:

kai: :thumbsup:

olivia: :thumbsup:

marta: thanks. i'll update the figma and drop a final copy in #launch-assets by EOD. if any objections speak now otherwise we'll ship this direction.
